action: Maintainers and vendors receiving reports from Anthropic: plan for public disclosure 30 days after a high- or critical-severity report (45 days for others) for reports sent on or after 1 January 2027, and fix or agree a remediation timeline early.
exec: Software vendors and open-source maintainers will have less time to fix flaws Anthropic reports before they are made public.
plain: Anthropic is shortening how long it waits before publishing security flaws it reports to software makers: 30 days for serious ones, down from 90. It applies to reports sent from 1 January 2027.

key_findings: Anthropic is shortening its coordinated vulnerability disclosure window from 90 days to 30 days for high- and critical-severity issues, and to 45 days for all other issues.
The new timelines apply to vulnerabilities reported on or after January 1, 2027; in-progress reports keep their existing deadlines.
High- and critical-severity reports filed more than 90 days ago that are past the current deadline and not yet public get an additional 30 days before publication on Anthropic's dashboard.
Anthropic's seven-day window for vulnerabilities under active exploitation remains unchanged.
recommendations: Where a flaw cannot be fixed in 30 or 45 days, Anthropic says it will work with the vendor on a remediation timeline.

summary: Anthropic says it is shortening its coordinated vulnerability disclosure window from 90 days to 30 days for high- and critical-severity issues, and to 45 days for all other issues. The new timelines apply to vulnerabilities reported on or after January 1, 2027; in-progress reports keep their existing deadlines. Its seven-day window for active exploitation remains unchanged.
title: Anthropic shortens its vulnerability disclosure window to 30 days for serious flaws

validation.note: Anthropic's own policy post read in full (published 16 November 2026). The Thai report from Blognone that surfaced the story returned 403 and was not read.
